doc.title: Bobby Watson interviewed by Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, January 19, 1996

title: Clarinet to saxophone: embouchure and fingering
summary: Moving from clarinet to saxophone is easier, apart from the embouchure and the octave key difference.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: You know that’s fabulous that you have these combination of skills. Am I correct in saying that many saxophone players say that the clarinet is the more difficult instrument? And if you start on that, switching to clarinet is easier?

Saxophone you mean. Starting on clarinet you mean and going to saxophone is easier? Yes it is. The only adjustment you have to make is your embouchure, because the clarinet is more of a tight smile and the saxophone is more of a frown. That took me a few years to make that. But most definitely, because with the clarinet, your fingers are the pads. So you have to be really exact. And like I say if you push the octave key, it’s not an octave key, it goes up a twelfth. So you have a whole different set of fingerings once you push that button. With the saxophone, you just push it and it goes up an octave, so it’s a lot easier.
